title: Turn on the cache autoload prefetchers (hart1 I-cache, hart0 I-cache, shared D-cache) from the loader through the ROM's own Config/Enable setters, with a runtime Suspend/Resume toggle
mechanism: All AUTOLOAD_CTRL registers read 0x2 (DONE set, ENA clear). The HAL has no setter, but the ROM exports Cache_Config/Enable_L1_CORE1_ICache_Autoload, the CORE0 pair, Cache_Config/Enable_L1_DCache_Autoload (4 sections) and Suspend/Resume variants. Call them from hart0 IRAM before hart1 is released: I-cache sections = kernel XIP window + PSRAM, trigger on miss; D-cache sections = Linux PSRAM minus the CMA/DMA pools. Expose Suspend/Resume through a hosted control op or an OpenSBI vendor call, so the effect can be A/B'd within one boot and escape the lottery.

title: Use the L1 cache access counters as the missing PMU, and point them at the per-boot lottery
mechanism: CACHE_L1_CACHE_ACS_CNT_CTRL_REG (0x2C000180) enables per-bus HIT/MISS/CONFLICT/NXTLVL_RD/WR counters. IBUS0 is hart0, IBUS1 is hart1, and DBUS0/1 are the two cores on the shared D-cache. The loader clears and enables them. A hart0 task snapshots them every 100 ms into SRAM (they wrap in ~14 s), and a Linux reader prints rates. Use it to find: (a) whether slow boots are D-cache miss/conflict boots; (b) whether .text..fast costs D-cache lines or I-cache capacity; (c) how much hart0 refill traffic contends with CPU0's XIP misses; (d) a ranking of .text..fast candidates by refills.

title: Pin the shared CPU clock at 320 MHz in firmware, and make the performance cpufreq default real
mechanism: The loader configures IDF DFS as max 320 / min 53, and Linux ondemand rewrites the minimum. On the S31 Wi-Fi's PM lock is NO_LIGHT_SLEEP, not CPU_FREQ_MAX. So whenever FreeRTOS IDLE runs, the rtos lock drops and the clock falls to Linux's floor. The Linux-side reading comes from a task that holds the lock, so it cannot see this. title: Lazy PIE/HWLoop ownership by trap-on-first-use, plus PIE-free musl string routines so most switches make no ecall
mechanism: The 'no trap-on-use' premise is wrong. IDF's own lazy enable, and patches 0053/0056, catch the PIE illegal instruction. On switch-in, leave the unit OFF unless the task is its last owner. The kernel publishes the incoming save-area PA with a plain store. A first-use trap (illegal-instruction traps reach M-mode anyway, medeleg 0xb100) makes OpenSBI save the old owner, restore the current task and enable the unit. Ecall only when switching away from the owner. PIE users today are only musl's memcpy64/strcmp/memchr/memcmp/memrchr (27 insns) and static busybox; replacing those with Zbb scalar code makes PIE use genuinely rare, and nothing traps on CPU1.

magnitude_estimate: About 2-12 us per user-involved switch. Roughly 0.1-0.6% of a core on the desktop, <=0.5% on Quake (all M-mode is 1.06%). Also SMP hygiene: no PIE bounces. Ship only if switchbench arm C and pp-boots show a net win (the user prefers keeping PIE).

title: Internal-SRAM text tier for the hottest straight-line kernel code (trap/IRQ spine, locks), using the unused 6,360 B of the OpenSBI window
mechanism: HP SRAM sits in front of no cache. Code there costs no I-cache or D-cache lines and no PSRAM bandwidth, and both harts see it. OpenSBI's trap path moved there and gained 4.9x on the switch. OpenSBI uses 10,024 of the reserved 16,384 B, leaving 6,360 B free with no cost to hart0. Link a .text.sram section: VMA a kernel VA mapped by one PTE (PAGE_KERNEL_EXEC) to PA ~0x2F07C400, copied by a word loop, with stvec switched afterwards. OpenSBI and the hart0 vCPU PMP grant S-mode RX on that range. Candidates are the 44 IRQ-spine functions (4,920 B, 5.8% of CPU0) plus the spinlock functions (486 B). Leave cache-resident loops in PSRAM: SRAM data access measured 6 cycles against 1 for a PSRAM hit. Run a Phase-0 timing first (flash vs PSRAM vs SRAM, cold and warm, on one body).

physics.reasoning:
The physics holds up better than the candidate's own evidence, but the size is small.

**What checks out.**
- **SRAM is uncached for fetch.** IDF's cache_ll.h for the S31 sets CACHE_LL_LEVEL_INT_MEM to 0 and CACHE_LL_LEVEL_NUMS to 1. So fetches from SRAM use no I-cache or D-cache lines and never miss.
- **SRAM code runs at hot-cache speed.** This is measured, not assumed. Since esp32s31.o moved into the SRAM window, the late_initcall in arch/riscv/kernel/esp32s31-ext.c prints its probes on every boot:
  - the phase-0 loop costs 1 cycle per iteration, even on the first, cold call;
  - 100 back-to-back empty ecalls cost 1,548-1,567 ns, against 1,716 ns when OpenSBI ran from hot I-cache flash.

title: Stop the display drivers interrupting CPU0 when nobody is listening: vblank hrtimer only while referenced, LCD VSYNC/TRANS_DONE masked unless hw_vblank, async PPA/GDMA completions polled
mechanism: lvdesk never waits for vblank or page flips (prompt_flip=1, wait_vblank=0), yet the 42-60 Hz vblank-emulation hrtimer runs for the pipe's whole life. VSYNC/TRANS_DONE (52/s) are only counted unless hw_vblank is set. Start and stop the timer from enable/disable_vblank; DRM's off-delay then stops it, and waiters re-arm it, which keeps Weston-style clients correct. title: Turn off 7.1's silently default-on HRTICK/HRTICK_DL (and A/B TTWU_QUEUE) through the plain sysctl_sched_features word
mechanism: CONFIG_HRTIMER_REARM_DEFERRED (def_bool through GENERIC_ENTRY) flips SCHED_FEAT HRTICK and HRTICK_DL to true; 6.18 and 7.0 had them false. With 2+ fair tasks queued, every pick arms a per-rq hrtimer at the EEVDF deadline (base slice 0.7 ms x2 = 1.4 ms). Each reprogram is an SBI ecall and each expiry an extra flash-resident timer IRQ plus a forced switch. XIP has no jump labels, so sched_feat() is a plain bit test on sysctl_sched_features (c086fad0, PA 0x5006FAD0; 0x1BE1FBDF -> 0x1BE1CBDF clears bits 12/13). Flip it by devmem to test, and ship as a core_param in our arch code or the <=7.0 default. TTWU_QUEUE (bit 15) also merits an A/B: with no SCHED_MC, every cross-CPU wake goes through the wakelist IPI.

title: Poll before wfi with TIF_POLLING_NRFLAG (bounded, adaptive, haltpoll-style), so cross-hart wakes skip the IPI and interrupt path
mechanism: riscv never defines HAVE_TIF_POLLING_NRFLAG, so every wake of an idle CPU is an IPI. On CPU1 that means FROM_CPU_3, FreeRTOS, monitor injection and a flash IRQ entry; on CPU0 a CLIC entry plus ipi_mux. Define the flag (one line). title: zswap as a bounded compressed tier in front of /swapfile (the design the capped-zram arm could not test)

title: Compositor-driven working-set handoff: lvdesk batch-pages-out background clients and idle daemons into contiguous swap on fullscreen entry, and prefetches them in bulk on intent (process_madvise PAGEOUT/COLD/WILLNEED)
mechanism: lvdesk knows intent: focus, occlusion, taskbar hover, menu launch, fullscreen enter and leave. On fullscreen entry, or when a client goes to the background under pressure, it calls process_madvise(MADV_PAGEOUT) on the client's anon VMAs, idle daemons (MADV_COLD) and its own LVGL pool (cold while fullscreen). Reclaim in VMA order gives consecutive swap slots and merged writes. On intent (hover or press, fullscreen exit) it calls MADV_WILLNEED over the same ranges, so readahead issues merged reads before the Expose redraw. Step 0: confirm slot contiguity from pagemap and request merging from /sys/block stat.

title: Settle whether the Sv32 walker snoops the D-cache; then either close the stale-PTE windows (SMP correctness) or delete the per-PTE writebacks, and batch publication at TLB-flush granularity
mechanism: The port writes back only in set_pte and set_pmd. Under CONFIG_SMP, ptep_get_and_clear is a bare xchg (the UP branch used set_pte). ptep_set_wrprotect is atomic_long_set, test_and_clear_young is a bit op, and new PTE pages are zeroed in cache. If the walker really does not snoop, COW, munmap reuse and reclaim aging can see stale entries, a candidate for the deferred Quake crash. Meanwhile every PTE that is published costs a double-issued sync plus stats, and fault-around writes back the same line up to 16 times. XIP text PTEs also each call flush_icache_mm. Step 1: an in-kernel self-test (write a PTE in cache only, sfence, touch) plus a fork/munmap hammer on both CPUs. Step 2: publish once per touched PTE page before the sfence, skip the icache flush for !pfn_valid XIP PTEs, and drop the always-on accounting (C33).

title: A polled SD host driver of our own: complete small reads synchronously in ->request (no IRQ, BH, kworker or sleep)
mechanism: A 4 KiB read today is CMD18, DATA_OVER, then a software-issued CMD12: ~3 IRQs, each with a BH run, then a mmc_complete kworker hop and a wake. That is two sleep/wake pairs at ~300 us each. Proposal: our own driver bound to espressif,esp32s31-dw-mshc, forked from dw_mmc/IDF sdmmc_host. For reads <=32 KiB it masks INTMASK, issues CMD18 with hardware auto-stop (SDMMC_CMD_SEND_STOP) or CMD23, spins on RINTSTS/IDSTS (~0.4 ms), and calls mmc_request_done before ->request returns. It sets MMC_CAP_DONE_COMPLETE. The faulting task never sleeps, and a CPU1 fault avoids the cross-hart completion wake. It falls back to the IRQ path after ~1-1.5 ms (card GC tails), and for writes and large reads.

title: musl libm without soft-double: integer floor/ceil/trunc/round/modf, single-precision FPU sinf/cosf/sincosf/atanf, libc linked against s31fp's bit-exact helpers

title: Take the last X round trip out of every SDL frame: xlite consumes the MIT-SHM put itself (or an engine or snapshot copy consumes it before the reply) and XSync returns without GetInputFocus, with a presented-counter handshake for back-pressure
mechanism: MIT-SHM requires the segment to be consumed before XSync returns; it does not require the server to be the one that consumes it. (1) In XShmPutImage, when XliteShmMap succeeds and the GC is plain, take xlite's existing XPutImage fast path: memcpy the rects from the client's own segment into the shared window buffer, then a one-way Damaged. Consuming synchronously in the caller cannot flicker the way adoption did. (2) XSync skips GetInputFocus when only Damaged is outstanding (request == shm_seq), after a non-blocking drain of s2c. (3) xshim bumps a 'presented' counter in the ring header; xlite falls back to a real XSync if lvdesk is more than one frame behind. Alternatives that keep the copy on CPU1: lvdesk copies by GDMA (210 vs 38 MB/s) before replying, then hashes afterwards; or xlite snapshots into a shared frame slot. Instrument first with an XSync latency histogram in xlite.

xlite.c:963-980 XSync = GetInputFocus; xlite_req.c:2808-2867 ShmPutImage queues only; xlite_req.c:3482-3540 PutImage fast path already consumes client-side
xshim.c:5357-5519 copy+hash before reply; 520-605 late present defers only expand/present

The libs and crosslayer lenses argue the net is far smaller (~0.5% Quake, 2-3% Doom), because the wait is mostly wake+copy and the client copy lands on CPU0. The histogram decides which estimate holds.

title: Test whether the per-boot lottery is physical page colour or placement: fingerprint each boot (PFNs of hot app text/SHM/scanout, CmaFree, IRQ rates, Wi-Fi state), and re-roll page-cache placement in-boot with drop_caches or allocator churn
mechanism: The caches are physically indexed. The 16 KB 2-way I-cache gives 2 colours per 4 KB page (4 if the TRM's 32 KB is right); the 64 KB 2-way D-cache gives 8. One Quake text page carries 17% of all CPU0 samples, and 17 pages cover 90% of the program's samples. Fresh processes map the same page-cache pages for the whole boot, which fits 'set at boot, holds for the run', and the eliminations so far never touched app page-cache placement. Tests: log PFN&1 and PFN&7 of hot app pages, the SHM segment and scanout via pagemap next to canary-boots/quake runs; within a boot, run, then echo 3 > drop_caches or churn 4-6 MB, then rerun. A mode flip inside one boot proves placement. Fixes: colour our own buffers (SHM, scanout, PPA intermediates), put hot kernel RAM text in one I-cache colour, or have the launcher re-fault a bad-colour hot text page. Also log ppa_table per boot, since the adaptive picker

physics.reasoning: PREMISE CHECKED AND PARTLY RIGHT. The caches really are physically indexed here: the cached PSRAM alias is 0x50000000-0x53FFFFFF and the L1 sits in front of the PSRAM MMU on the bus address, so PFN low bits are the index. The geometry in the repo (bootloader/sdkconfig: CONFIG_CACHE_L1_ICACHE_SIZE=0x4000, LINE_SIZE=64, 2-way; DCACHE 0x10000) gives exactly the candidate's colour counts: I-cache way = 8 KB, 128 sets, index PA[12:6] -> 1 colour bit = 2 colours; D-cache way = 32 KB, 512 sets, index PA[14:6] -> 3 bits = 8 colours; per colour bin, capacity is 2 pages. The candidate's page numbers also check out against the raw samples in /Users/gadyke/esp32-s31-linux/artifacts/quake/h1s-062518/pcs.
